# Screening against CelesTrak's SOCRATES

<!-- Generated by tools/screening_report.py; do not edit. -->

CelesTrak's [SOCRATES](https://celestrak.org/SOCRATES/) lists, for a week, the approaches within 5 km of the objects it screens, from SGP4 on the GP element sets of its time. This page compares keepout's screening of the same element sets with SOCRATES's list. SOCRATES is an independent implementation, so an approach both find with the same TCA, range and speed is a check of keepout's propagation, search and TCA refinement.

**1269 of 1274 compared approaches agree with SOCRATES within tolerance; the 5 others trace to 2 objects whose element sets differ from the ones SOCRATES used.**

Data: USSPACECOM/18 SDS via Space-Track.org, retrieved from CelesTrak (celestrak.org) on 2026-10-06; the public catalog and the SOCRATES report sorted by minimum range (see `tests/screening/data/NOTICE`).

## How the comparison was made

keepout screened with [`screen`](reference/screening.md#keepout.screening.screen) and its defaults: the 5 km sphere (as in CelesTrak's SOCRATES), 7 days from 2026-10-06 00:00 UTC (SOCRATES's window), element sets at most 30 days older than the window's end and 3 days newer than its start.

SOCRATES gives each object's epoch only as days from it to TCA (DSE, three decimals: 43 s), and CelesTrak serves only the latest element sets, so only some approaches can be compared. Of the 186229 approaches of SOCRATES's report (TCA 2026-10-06 00:00 to 2026-10-12 23:59 UTC), 1275 have both objects in the public catalog with the epochs SOCRATES used. Of these, 1274 are compared and 1 is left out, as screening drops an element set of its pair (see [Not compared](#not-compared)).

The 192 objects that SOCRATES lists first in a pair are screened as primaries against all 306 objects of those approaches. An approach depends on its own pair only, so the rest of the catalog changes nothing.

Each SOCRATES approach is matched with keepout's approach of the same pair whose TCA is nearest, within 60 s. *Fast* approaches are those of 1 km/s or more by SOCRATES; the others, mostly formation flyers, are *slow*.

## Tolerances

| Approaches | TCA | Range | Relative speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast (>= 1 km/s) | 1 ms | 0.501 m | 0.501 m/s |
| slow (< 1 km/s) | 500 ms | 0.501 m | 0.501 m/s |

SOCRATES prints TCA (UTC) to the millisecond, `TCA_RANGE` in km and `TCA_RELATIVE_SPEED` in km/s with three decimals, so rounding alone leaves up to 0.5 ms, 0.5 m and 0.5 m/s; read in these units, every approach within tolerance agrees to half the last printed digit. Range and speed are allowed 1 mm and 1 mm/s more, keepout's accuracy target. A fast approach's TCA is allowed 1 ms: the rounding, and as much again for the two TCA searches. A slow pair's range hardly changes for seconds around its minimum, which leaves its TCA ill-conditioned: it is allowed 0.5 s, and moving TCA by the differences found changes the range by 0.0003 m at most.

## Agreement

| Approaches | Compared | Within tolerance | Worst TCA | Worst range | Worst relative speed | Range change over the TCA difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fast (>= 1 km/s) | 266 | 261 | 0.493 ms | 0.49565 m | 0.49797 m/s | 0.036 m |
| slow (< 1 km/s) | 1008 | 1008 | 324.653 ms | 0.49998 m | 0.49897 m/s | 0.0003 m |

Worst: the largest difference between keepout and SOCRATES among the approaches within tolerance; the last column is how much the range changes when TCA moves by the TCA difference (v² Δt² / 2r, with r the range at keepout's minimum). The approaches outside tolerance are under [Differences](#differences).

## Differences

| Pair | SOCRATES TCA (UTC) | SOCRATES range | SOCRATES speed | keepout TCA - SOCRATES | keepout range | keepout speed | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 47834 - 38513 | 2026-10-11 23:25:37.317 | 2452 m | 14152 m/s | 354.374 ms | 3092.539 m | 14152.101 m/s | other element set of STARLINK-2424 |
| 47804 - 100379 | 2026-10-09 20:20:04.903 | 3605 m | 14765 m/s | -227.884 ms | 3579.706 m | 14764.928 m/s | other element set of STARLINK-38284 |
| 66193 - 100379 | 2026-10-10 22:57:49.178 | 4252 m | 14751 m/s | -306.241 ms | 3496.828 m | 14751.022 m/s | other element set of STARLINK-38284 |
| 66193 - 100379 | 2026-10-10 23:44:42.575 | 4475 m | 14759 m/s | -308.730 ms | 5174.446 m (not reported: outside the volume) | 14758.531 m/s | other element set of STARLINK-38284 |
| 63707 - 100379 | 2026-10-09 12:28:05.695 | 4902 m | 14701 m/s | -206.732 ms | 5140.813 m (not reported: outside the volume) | 14701.448 m/s | other element set of STARLINK-38284 |

- **other element set of STARLINK-2424**: STARLINK-2424 (47834) has one comparable approach, with FENGYUN 1C DEB (38513), and it differs; the ten other comparable approaches of 38513 agree. SOCRATES used an element set of 47834 with the same epoch (to DSE's 43 s resolution) but evidently different elements.
- **other element set of STARLINK-38284**: All four comparable approaches of STARLINK-38284 (100379) differ, by a TCA growing with the time since its epoch (0.21 s after 6.3 days, 0.31 s after 7.8 days). A B* 3.4 % lower than the snapshot's reproduces all four to 2.3 ms and 2.8 m: SOCRATES used an element set with the same epoch (to DSE's 43 s resolution) but different elements.

## Found by keepout only

Formation flyers can have two range minima per orbit, minutes apart, with a maximum at most a few metres higher between them. keepout reports every local minimum inside the volume; SOCRATES lists only one of the two once they come close. The last column gives the time to the nearest other approach keepout reports for the pair.

## Not compared

- **40211 approaches with an object outside the public catalog**: SOCRATES screens the whole catalog of Space-Track.org; CelesTrak publishes only part of it.
- **144743 approaches whose objects are in the public catalog with other element sets**: the snapshot was downloaded hours after SOCRATES's data cut-off, and most objects had new element sets by then.
- **Pairs SOCRATES does not list.** SOCRATES does not report every pair that comes within 5 km: TerraSAR-X (31698) and TanDEM-X (36605), for example, fly in formation a few hundred metres apart and are not in its report. keepout's approaches are compared only for the pairs SOCRATES lists.

1 approach has an object `screen` left out, with its defaults:
